phases.title: Accounts and keys
phases.goal: You own a verified Play developer account, a backed-up signing key, the legal details on the site, and one password-manager page that holds every id.

items.title: Create the Google Play Console developer account
items.time: 20 min + days of ID checking · $25 once
items.why: Google must verify who you are before femio can be published. The check can take a few days, so start it first.
steps: Open play.google.com/console and sign in with the Google account that will own femio for good (not a work account you might lose).
Choose 'Yourself' (a personal developer account).
Pay the one-time $25.
Complete identity verification: upload a government ID; Google may also send a letter or a code. Use your legal name and your Cairo address.
Wait for the verification result (it can take a few days).
items.doneWhen: The Play Console shows the account as Verified.
items.risk: A personal account must later run a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days (see closed-test-window). That is the price of not needing a company number; plan for it.

items.title: Create the upload signing key and back it up twice
items.why: The key proves every future update of the app comes from you. If you lose it, femio has to be re-created as a new app.
steps: Make sure the folder E:\_Private exists (create it in File Explorer if not).
Open PowerShell on your PC and run the keytool command in the paste box below.
When it asks, choose a long passphrase and type your name.
Save the passphrase in your password manager under the name 'femio upload key'.
Copy the file femio-upload-keystore.jks to a second place: an offline drive or a password-manager attachment.
Check that both copies open in File Explorer and have the same size.
items.doneWhen: Two copies of femio-upload-keystore.jks exist in different places and the passphrase is in your password manager.
items.risk: Never put the .jks file or the passphrase inside the repository or in chat.

items.title: Point the app build at your key (key.properties)
items.why: Without this file the release build signs with a debug key, which Google Play will not accept for real uploads.
steps: In apps/mobile/android, copy key.properties.example to a new file named key.properties.
Open key.properties in a text editor and type the path to the .jks file and the passwords you chose.
Save. The file is ignored by git; never commit it.
In PowerShell go to apps/mobile and run: flutter build appbundle --release
Read the end of the output: it must finish without the word 'debug' in the signing line.
items.doneWhen: flutter build appbundle --release finishes without 'debug' signing.
items.risk: If the build fails, copy the last 20 lines to a session and say 'the release build fails'; do not edit the gradle files yourself.

items.title: Fill the three legal placeholders and choose the support email
items.why: The privacy page and the store texts show your name, a contact address and a date. Until they are filled, the pages show highlighted placeholders.
steps: Decide the legal entity text: KM Digital Labs and its registration number, or your name as a sole trader.
Decide the privacy contact email: one address you actually read. The same address becomes the Play contact email and the support email in the store texts.
Decide the effective date (the launch week).
Tell a session the three values (or edit apps/web/src/lib/legal/placeholders.ts yourself): 'Fill the legal placeholders: entity ..., email ..., date ...'.
items.doneWhen: apps/web/src/lib/legal/placeholders.ts holds the three real values (you confirm after the website goes live in phone-check).
items.risk: The store full descriptions also contain the marker [SUPPORT EMAIL: owner action 3]; it is replaced in the store-lint item, not here.

items.title: Pause Supabase and delete the old femio-cms Vercel project
items.why: Version 3 has no database and no CMS. Leaving the old cloud running is a cost and a liability.
steps: Only if you ever edited translations in the old CMS translation portal: in Supabase open the SQL editor, run: select key, locale, value from ui_strings where status = 'human_reviewed' and locale <> 'en' ; download the result as CSV and send it to a session to merge.
Open supabase.com, choose the femio project, then Settings, then General, then click 'Pause project' and confirm.
Open vercel.com, find the project femio-cms and delete it (Settings, then Delete Project). Keep the project 'femio' (the website).
items.doneWhen: The Supabase dashboard says Paused and Vercel shows one femio project (the website).
items.risk: Export the translations first if you ever used the portal: a paused project is recoverable, but a deleted Vercel project is not.

items.title: Create the 'femio growth' page in your password manager
items.why: Every measurement and ad account produces an id. One page keeps them together, and you can find them again if you lose track.
steps: In your password manager create a secure note named 'femio growth'.
Add empty lines for: Search Console property, GA4 Measurement ID (G- id), Tag Manager container (GTM- id), Meta Pixel ID, AdSense publisher id (pub- id), social handles.
Fill each line as the later items produce it. Never paste an id into chat; a session only ever needs the public ones (G-, GTM-, pub-), and you put those into Vercel yourself.
items.doneWhen: The note exists with the empty lines ready.
items.guide: docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/04_OWNER_GUIDE_GROWTH_A_TO_Z.md 'Where things live'; the lost-page row of its trouble table

phases.title: Website go-live checks
phases.goal: femioapp.com serves the version 3 site, your phone shows it correctly, main is protected, and the pages you approved are published.

items.title: Ask a session to merge version 3 into main and deploy
items.why: The website the world sees is whatever is on the main branch. Until the merge, femioapp.com still shows the old design.
steps: Open Claude Code in the femio repo.
Say: 'Merge the v3 branch into main and deploy'. The branch today is claude/femio-repo-study-planning-88d7c9.
The session runs the gate, merges and pushes. Vercel then builds main.
Open vercel.com, project femio, Deployments: wait until the newest deployment shows Ready.
Ask the session to run the sitemap check on femioapp.com (the command is in the paste box).
items.doneWhen: The newest Vercel deployment of main is Ready and the sitemap check passes.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: Merge the v3 branch into main and deploy

items.risk: If the site still shows the old design, Vercel built an older commit: tell a session 'redeploy main'. Do branch-protection after this item, or the session's push will be refused (it would open a pull request instead).

items.title: Clean the Vercel environment variables
items.why: The build does not read old Supabase, Sentry, PostHog, CMS or notification variables, and a stray value is a liability.
steps: Open vercel.com, project femio, then Settings, then Environment Variables.
Delete every Supabase, Sentry, PostHog, CMS and VAPID variable.
Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL. Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION and NEXT_PUBLIC_CRISIS_DIRECTORY_URL if they exist (both are optional).
If you are unsure what a variable is, take a screenshot and show it to a session before deleting.
items.doneWhen: Only NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and the two optional variables remain.
items.risk: The runbook list predates the growth work: later you will deliberately add NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID (gtm-vercel) and NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT (adsense-verify). Those are expected. Later variables that are expected: NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID (phase 3) and NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT plus three NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_SLOT_* (phase 4).

items.title: Protect the main branch on GitHub
items.why: Agents will open pull requests every week. Main must accept nothing without you pressing Merge.
steps: Open github.com, your femio repository, Settings, Branches, then 'Add branch ruleset' (or 'Add rule' on the older screen). Name it main and target the branch main.
Tick 'Require a pull request before merging' and set approvals to 1.
Tick 'Require status checks to pass' and add the Vercel check, and the check named gate if the gate runs in Actions.
Tick 'Block force pushes'. Save.
Open Settings, Actions, General, Workflow permissions: choose 'Read repository contents' and tick 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests'. Save.
Test it: ask a session to push to main.
items.doneWhen: GitHub refuses the push with 'protected branch', and the session opens a pull request that you can Merge.
items.risk: GitHub menu labels change; if a label differs, keep the intent: pull request required, 1 approval, no force push [verify in console].

items.title: Check the live site on your phone (calculator, privacy, help-now, share card)
items.why: Your own eyes on a real phone are the only test that counts for the first launch.
steps: On your phone open femioapp.com/ar/calculators/fertile-window. Tap a day: the fertile window draws on the calendar and the Hijri date shows under each day.
Open femioapp.com/ar/privacy: your entity, email and date appear where the highlighted placeholders were.
Open femioapp.com/en/help-now, choose Egypt: the numbers appear with their sources.
Share any article link in WhatsApp: the preview card shows the plum femio image.
items.doneWhen: All four checks look right on your phone.
items.risk: If anything is wrong, write one line to a session, for example: 'On the privacy page in Arabic, the date is missing'.

items.title: Say 'publish' on the legal pages and the Arabic articles you approve
items.time: as long as you want · free
items.why: You are the named medical reviewer; nothing medical goes live until you say so.
steps: Ask a session for the list of legal pages and Arabic articles waiting for your approval.
Read the ones you want to release now.
Say 'publish' for each page or article you approve.

For docs/content/articles/pcos-treatment-options-to-discuss.md: the AI reviewer would not sign it until a clinician confirms letrozole availability for ovulation induction in Egypt and Saudi Arabia and whether to add an OHSS warning. Read docs/content/reviews/2026-10-28-pcos-set.md, then publish, fix or hold.

Note two cited pages that moved: the ASRM 2021 page in docs/compliance/FERTILITY_AWARENESS_SAFETY.md now returns 404 (a 2026 version replaced it) and the NHS infertility-treatment page passed its review date. Tell a session whether to refresh them.
items.doneWhen: Every page you approved is live and the PCOS guide is published, fixed or on hold by your word.
items.risk: Do not hurry the PCOS guide: it contains a medical claim only you can sign.

items.title: Answer the four content questions (three Arabic, one red-flag)
items.why: Tone, scope and a medical claim are your calls. A session records each as a decision and applies it.
steps: Question 9a: the Arabic guides drop the English lines on donor sperm, same-sex couples, parenting alone and home insemination. Say 'keep' (the default, for Egypt and Saudi readers) or 'restore'.
Question 9b: the lay term تكيّس المبايض is used in guides, app and store instead of the glossary term المبيض المتعدد الكيسات. Say 'keep the lay term' (default) or 'switch'.
Question 9c: in the Ramadan guide, say whether the person she asks about fasting is 'المرجع الديني' or 'أهل العلم الشرعي'.

Question 10 (register MR-29): the app and site list five Hear Her warning signs. Bleeding and reduced movements are standard additions but have no source in docs/compliance. Name an NHS or RCOG page for them, or say 'no'.
Send the four one-word answers to a session in one message.
items.doneWhen: A session has recorded all four answers (decision record) and applied them.
items.risk: For question 10 do not name a source you have not opened; an invented source is worse than 'no'.

items.title: Listen to the calculator with the NVDA screen reader
items.why: A screen reader is heard, not tested in code. The keyboard part is already automated; only your ears can say whether it reads well.
steps: Install NVDA (free) from nvaccess.org (about 15 min).
Open femioapp.com/ar/calculators/fertile-window.
Press Tab until a day is read out. Use the arrow keys to move between days, then press Enter.
Note whether NVDA reads: the full date on each day, the result sentence after Enter, and nothing twice.
Write what you heard in testing-results/2026-10-28-calendar-a11y/nvda-notes.md. A session turns it into fixes.
items.doneWhen: nvda-notes.md exists with your three observations.

items.title: Create the one-question feedback form
items.why: It is the only feedback channel; the app has no analytics. The Settings link 'Tell us one thing' opens it.
steps: Create a form in any form tool you like.
Add one free-text question: 'What is one thing femio should do better?'
Add a visible warning above it: 'Please do not include health details.'
Copy the form's public link.
Give the link to a session: 'Here is the feedback form URL: ...' so it is wired to the Settings link and the site.
items.doneWhen: The form opens in a private browser window and its link is wired in the app and site by a session.
items.risk: The form must warn about health details, or the Data safety answer 'no data collected' is weakened.

phases.title: Measurement: Search Console, GA4, Tag Manager, consent banner, Meta
phases.goal: Google can see the site, GA4 and Meta count visits only after a visitor taps Allow, and you have proved it in Tag Manager Preview.

items.title: Add femioapp.com to Google Search Console and submit the sitemap
items.why: It is the only place that shows which Google searches show femio. Free, no cookie, no banner. The weekly routine R1 reads it.
steps: Open search.google.com/search-console and click 'Add property'.
Choose 'Domain', type femioapp.com and click Continue.
Google shows a TXT record string. Copy it.
Open vercel.com, your team, Domains, femioapp.com, DNS Records, Add: Type TXT, Name @ (leave blank if Vercel says so), Value = the string, then Save.
Back in Search Console press Verify. If it fails wait an hour (DNS can take up to two or three days) and press Verify again.
In Search Console open Sitemaps, paste https://femioapp.com/sitemap.xml and Submit.
Settings (gear), Users and permissions: add the Google account you use with the Ahrefs connector as Full user, if it is different from the one you used here.
Write the property name on your 'femio growth' page.
items.doneWhen: Sitemaps shows Success with a page count; after 2-3 days Performance shows impressions.
items.risk: Do not delete the TXT record after verifying; you can lose verification. If DNS is awkward use the URL-prefix property with the HTML tag: copy only the content value into Vercel as NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION and Redeploy.

items.title: Request indexing for the key pages in Search Console
items.why: It asks Google to look at your most important pages first instead of waiting.
steps: In Search Console use the search bar at the top (URL Inspection) and paste https://femioapp.com/ar then choose 'Request indexing'.
Repeat for /en, the 7 Arabic calculators, /ar/app, and each Arabic wedge article as it ships. There is a daily quota: do the highest-priority pages first.
Optional (10 min): in Bing Webmaster Tools choose 'Import from Google Search Console'.
items.doneWhen: Each listed URL shows 'Indexing requested' in Search Console.
items.risk: Hitting the daily quota is normal; continue the next day.

items.title: Create the Google Analytics 4 property and web data stream
items.why: GA4 counts visits to the site (only after consent). Its id is carried by Tag Manager, not pasted into the site.
steps: Open analytics.google.com, Admin (gear, bottom left), Create, Account. Name it KM Digital Labs. Untick every data-sharing box except 'Technical support'. Next. [verify in console]
Property: name 'femio website', time zone (GMT+02:00) Cairo, currency US Dollar. Next. [verify in console]

Business details: industry Health, size Small. Objectives: tick 'Examine user behavior' only. Create. Accept the terms (country Egypt). Also open the Data Processing Terms and accept them (needed for visitors in the EEA). [verify in console]

Data stream: choose Web, URL https://femioapp.com, stream name femioapp.com. Under Enhanced measurement keep it ON but open the gear and untick 'Form interactions' and 'Site search'. Create stream. [verify in console]
Copy the Measurement ID (starts with G-) to your 'femio growth' page. Do NOT install the tag Google offers; Tag Manager carries it.
items.doneWhen: Admin, Data streams shows the stream with your G- id. (No data arrives until gtm-publish.)
items.risk: ADR-075 was accepted on 2026-10-28, so measuring the website is allowed. The app is never measured.

items.title: Turn off Google signals, set retention, filter your own visits
items.why: This is a health site: no cross-device profiles, shortest sensible retention, and your own visits kept out of the numbers.
steps: Admin, Data settings, Data collection: turn OFF 'Google signals'. [verify in console]
Data retention: set 14 months. [verify in console]
If offered, untick EEA countries under 'Granular location and device data'. [verify in console]
Admin, Data streams, your stream, Configure tag settings, Define internal traffic: add your home IP address. [verify in console]
Admin, Data filters: set the 'Internal traffic' filter to Active. [verify in console]
Admin, Property access management: add the account used by the routines as Viewer (same account as Search Console step 'Users and permissions').
items.doneWhen: Google signals shows OFF, retention 14 months, and the internal-traffic filter is Active.
items.risk: If your home IP changes your own visits will show again; check on your phone with mobile data when testing.

items.title: Create the Google Tag Manager account and container
items.why: One Tag Manager script on the site carries every other tag, and consent decides when each tag may fire.
steps: Open tagmanager.google.com and click 'Create account': name KM Digital Labs, country Egypt. [verify in console]
Container name femioapp.com, platform Web. Create and accept the terms.
Copy the container id (starts with GTM-) from the top bar to your 'femio growth' page. Close the install dialog (a session installs the code).
Left menu Admin, Container settings: tick 'Enable consent overview'. Save. [verify in console]
items.doneWhen: The container exists, its GTM- id is on your 'femio growth' page, and the consent overview is enabled.
items.risk: Do not paste the install snippet anywhere; the site code is already built and stays inert until you add the id (gtm-vercel).

items.title: Import the ready-made container (GA4, seven events, consent rules)
items.why: The file holds the GA4 tag, seven event tags, triggers, variables and consent settings, so you do not type 20 things by hand. It contains none of your ids.
steps: In Tag Manager open Admin, then Import Container.
Choose the file docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/gtm/femio-container.json.
Workspace: Existing, Default Workspace. Choose Merge, then 'Rename conflicting'. Confirm.
Open Variables, User-Defined, 'const · GA4 measurement id'. Replace the placeholder value with your G- id from the ga4 item. Save.
Check that the tags list shows 'GA4 · configuration' and seven 'GA4 · ...' event tags.
items.doneWhen: The workspace lists the GA4 configuration tag and the seven event tags, and the constant variable holds your G- id.
items.risk: If the import shows a validation error, the export format changed since 2026-10-28: give a session the exact message. The manual route (guide D3-D6) builds the same things by hand.

items.title: Create and publish the consent banner (EN, AR, FR, ES)
items.why: Every tag must wait for the visitor's Allow, and the ad units fill only after the banner grants ad_storage (the code checks it). AdSense's own message shows in Europe, the UK and Switzerland only, so with route A alone a reader in Cairo or Riyadh never sees an ad.
steps: Decide the route first: route B (a free certified consent tool shown to every visitor) is the one that works for Egypt and Saudi Arabia; route A (AdSense's own message) only ever asks European visitors.
Route A (preferred; needs the AdSense account from adsense-apply and the script from adsense-mount): open adsense.google.com, 'Privacy & messaging'. [verify in console]
Choose GDPR, 'Create message', site femioapp.com, languages English, Arabic, French, Spanish.
Under consent options tick 'Do not consent' so declining is one tap.
Styling: plum #8A3572 for the button, cream #FBF7F3 for the background. Publish.
Create the US state regulations message (opt-out) the same way and publish.

Route B if AdSense is not ready: use a free certified consent tool (CookieYes, Cookiebot or similar). Check its free tier's page limit against about 160 pages. Add femioapp.com, enable Google Consent Mode v2 and IAB TCF v2.3, languages EN/AR/FR/ES, copy the script URL (never a key), and tell a session: 'Mount this CMP snippet before GTM'.
Verify in gtm-preview that the banner also updates Consent Mode for the GA4 tag; if it does not, use route B.
items.doneWhen: A banner appears on femioapp.com with Allow and decline, in all four languages, and gtm-preview confirms consent flips the tags.
items.risk: Route A (AdSense Privacy & messaging) shows its dialog in the EEA/UK/Switzerland only; femio's ad units fill only after a consent update, so for Egypt and Saudi Arabia you need route B (a certified tool shown to everyone, Consent Mode v2 on). Route B also lets you finish phase 3 before AdSense exists.

items.title: Put the Tag Manager id into Vercel yourself
items.why: The site sends nothing to Tag Manager until this variable exists. You do it so the id never travels through chat.
steps: Open vercel.com, project femio-web, Settings, Environment Variables.
Add a variable named NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID with your GTM- id as the value. Tick Production and Preview. Save.
Open Deployments, the latest one, the three-dot menu, Redeploy.
Tell a session: 'GTM id is set in Vercel; verify consent on the preview'.
items.doneWhen: The redeploy finished and the session confirms the site loads the container only after the banner choice.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: GTM id is set in Vercel; verify consent on the preview

items.risk: The guide names the project femio-web while the launch guide calls it femio: use whichever project serves femioapp.com.

items.title: Prove consent works with Tag Manager Preview
items.why: This is the one test that shows no tag fires before the visitor agrees. Do it yourself once so you understand it.
steps: In Tag Manager press Preview, enter https://femioapp.com/ar and click Connect.
A new tab opens with a 'Tag Assistant connected' badge. In the Tag Assistant window open the Consent tab: every type must read Denied on load.
Check that the GA4 tag sits under 'Tags not fired'.
On the site banner press Allow. The Consent tab flips analytics_storage to Granted and the GA4 configuration tag appears under 'Tags fired'.
Open a calculator and tap a day: calculator_open then calculator_used appear, with only calculator_slug as a parameter.
items.doneWhen: Nothing fires before Allow and everything described above fires after Allow.
items.risk: If any tag fires before Allow, stop and tell a session exactly which tag; it is a missing consent setting on that tag.

items.title: Publish the Tag Manager version and see your first visit in GA4
items.why: Until you publish, the container does nothing on the live site.
steps: In Tag Manager click Submit. Version name: v1 consent + GA4. Publish.
Open analytics.google.com, Reports, Realtime.
On another device (phone on mobile data) open femioapp.com/ar, press Allow on the banner.
Watch for your visit in Realtime within a minute.
items.doneWhen: GA4 Realtime shows a visit from another device.
items.risk: Your own IP is filtered by ga4-privacy: use mobile data on the phone, not home wifi.

items.title: Set up the Meta business portfolio, Facebook Page and Pixel dataset
items.why: A pixel shows which Facebook and Instagram posts bring readers and builds an audience for organic reach. Meta may restrict a health domain to Core Setup; the plan already assumes it.
steps: Open business.facebook.com and 'Create a business portfolio': name KM Digital Labs, your name, your business email. Confirm the email. [verify in console]
Settings, Business assets, Pages: add or create the Facebook Page named femio, category 'Health & wellness website'. Use the bio from 04_GROWTH_PACK.md section 1, Arabic first. [verify in console]

Settings, Data sources, Datasets (older screen: Pixels), Add: name femioapp.com, 'Set up manually'. Copy the Dataset/Pixel ID to your 'femio growth' page. Do not install the code; Tag Manager carries it. [verify in console]

Events Manager, the dataset, Settings: 'Automatic advanced matching' OFF and 'Track events automatically without code' OFF. Read what Meta applied under Data sharing restrictions; Core Setup is expected. [verify in console]

Business Settings, Brand safety and suitability, Domains, Add femioapp.com. Verify by DNS TXT record (Vercel, Domains, DNS Records, like Search Console) or give the meta tag content value to a session: 'Set Meta domain verification tag'. [verify in console]
items.doneWhen: The dataset exists, its id is on your 'femio growth' page, and the domain shows Verified.
items.risk: 'Core Setup' is expected for a health domain; nothing to change.

items.title: Add the three Meta Pixel tags in Tag Manager
items.why: The pixel fires only three simple events and only after the visitor allows advertising storage.
steps: In Tag Manager, Tags, New. Search the Community Template Gallery for the Facebook Pixel template (by Meta) or the official Meta Pixel template. [verify in console]
Tag 1: Pixel ID = yours, event PageView, trigger All Pages. Consent settings: require ad_storage and ad_user_data.
Tag 2: event ViewContent on the triggers article_read and calculator_open. No parameters. Same consent settings.
Tag 3: event Lead on the trigger get_app_click. No parameters. Same consent settings.
Press Preview as in gtm-preview: nothing fires before Allow; after it, PageView appears in Events Manager, Test events, within a minute.
Submit and publish as version v2 meta pixel.
items.doneWhen: Events Manager, Overview shows PageView from femioapp.com with 'Browser' as the source.
items.risk: A tag that fires before Allow is a missing consent setting: stop and tell a session which tag.

phases.title: Website ads: AdSense, units, blocking list, ads.txt
phases.goal: AdSense approves femioapp.com, two labelled ads show below the fold on articles, sensitive ad categories are blocked, and ads.txt is found.

items.title: Apply to Google AdSense with femioapp.com
items.time: 20 min + days to weeks of waiting · free
items.why: Ads are the second income line for the website. Apply when the site has steady readers: the plan's threshold is about 1,000 sessions a week or 8 weeks after launch, whichever comes first (a hypothesis, Google publishes no number).
steps: Open adsense.google.com and click 'Get started'.
Enter your site femioapp.com, country Egypt, and accept the terms.
Google shows a code snippet containing your publisher id (starts with pub-). Write the id on your 'femio growth' page. Do not paste the snippet anywhere.
If you want to use route A of the consent banner, this account must exist first.
items.doneWhen: The AdSense account exists, the site is added, and the pub- id is on your 'femio growth' page.
items.risk: 'Site not ready' or 'Low value content': wait two weeks of content updates and re-apply; the pages are sourced and signed, which is what the review looks for.

items.title: Fill the AdSense payments information
items.why: Google pays only after identity and address are confirmed; the payment threshold is $100.
steps: In AdSense open Payments, then Payments info.
Enter your name and address exactly as on your bank account and ID.

Add the payment method AdSense offers. For Egypt the plan expects a wire transfer to your bank, in the same name as the account. Confirm in this screen, because that is not verified against Google's own payment table.
Expect a PIN letter by post at your address before the first payment, so the postal address must be real.
items.doneWhen: Payments info shows complete, with a payment method added.
items.risk: A name that does not match the bank account delays or blocks payment.

items.title: Put the AdSense publisher id into Vercel and redeploy
items.why: The ad code is built (R6.8) and stays off until this one variable exists. Setting it makes article and hub pages load the AdSense script (which also carries the verification) and makes femioapp.com/ads.txt print your line.
steps: vercel.com, project that serves femioapp.com, Settings, Environment Variables.
Add NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT = ca-pub-… (the id exactly as AdSense prints it in the ad code, with the ca- prefix), for Production and Preview. Save.
Deployments, latest, the ⋯ menu, Redeploy.
Open femioapp.com/ads.txt: it must show 'google.com, pub-…, DIRECT, f08c47fec0942fa0'.
items.doneWhen: femioapp.com/ads.txt shows your pub- id; view-source of an article shows a script from pagead2.googlesyndication.com.
items.risk: Ids go into Vercel, never into chat. Without the ca- prefix the site ignores the value (it is validated) and nothing loads.

items.title: Set the AdSense id in Vercel, press Verify, wait for the review email
items.time: 10 min + days to weeks of waiting · free
items.why: This is the step that asks Google to review the site.
steps: Open vercel.com, project femio-web, Settings, Environment Variables.
Add NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT with your pub- id (Production and Preview). Save.
Deployments, latest, the three-dot menu, Redeploy.
Back in AdSense press Verify for femioapp.com.
Wait for the review email (days to weeks).
items.doneWhen: AdSense shows the site as Ready (approved).
items.risk: 'Policy violation: sensitive' on a page: tell a session the URL; it removes units from that page and appeals with the review trail.

items.title: Check that ads.txt is live and AdSense finds it
items.why: ads.txt tells ad buyers that you authorise Google to sell your ads; AdSense shows a warning until it finds the file. It is not in the owner guides: it comes from Google's own help page. On 2026-10-29 the working tree (uncommitted, built by a session) already has a /ads.txt route that prints the line from NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT, so after adsense-verify it may need no extra work. The route is built: femioapp.com/ads.txt prints the line as soon as the publisher id is in Vercel.
steps: After adsense-verify is done and the site is redeployed, open https://femioapp.com/ads.txt in a browser. It should show one line of the shape in the paste box, with your own pub- id.
If the page is empty or says only a comment, tell a session: 'Add an ads.txt file at the site root for my AdSense publisher id pub-...' (real id) and wait for the deploy.
In AdSense open Sites, click femioapp.com and compare the line with the 'Ads.txt snippet' (Copy). [verify in console]
Click 'Check for updates' for femioapp.com.
items.doneWhen: femioapp.com/ads.txt shows the line, and AdSense stops showing Not found / Unauthorized for the site.

paste.label: Line shape (copy the real one from AdSense)
Session sentence (suggested wording)
paste.value: Add an ads.txt file at the site root for my AdSense publisher id pub-...

items.guide: Not in the owner guides; added from https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/12171612
items.risk: Changes can take a few days to appear, up to a month for sites with few ad requests. A typo in the id makes the status Unauthorized. If the /ads.txt route was not merged, the session must merge it first.

items.title: Turn Auto ads off and create the three ad units
items.why: femio places ads itself: two on articles, one on hubs, never near the calculator. Auto ads would put them everywhere.
steps: After approval, open AdSense, Ads, By site: turn Auto ads OFF for femioapp.com. [verify in console]
Ads, By ad unit, Display ads: create a responsive unit named article-mid. [verify in console]
Create a second responsive unit named article-end.
Create a third responsive unit named hub-top.
Copy only the slot numbers (digits) of each unit.
Then do adsense-place: the three slot digits go into Vercel yourself.
items.doneWhen: Three units exist, Auto ads is OFF, and a session has the three slot numbers.
items.risk: No ad may render before the consent banner is live (02_MONETIZATION.md section 1.2).

items.title: Put the three slot ids into Vercel and redeploy; a session checks page speed
items.why: Each placement reads its own slot id, so you can switch one off later by deleting one variable. The placements themselves are already in the code: two per article below the fold, one on the Learn index and the condition hubs, none on calculators, help-now or legal pages.
steps: vercel.com, Settings, Environment Variables: add NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_SLOT_ARTICLE_MID, NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_SLOT_ARTICLE_END and NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_SLOT_HUB_TOP, each = the digits of that unit.
Redeploy.
Open an article on your phone, press Allow on the banner, scroll: a labelled ad after the first section and one after the sources. Decline on another device: no ad, no empty box.
Tell a session: 'AdSense slots are set; run Lighthouse on an article with ads'. It must stay at or above 85 performance.
items.doneWhen: An article shows two labelled ads below the fold after Allow and none after decline; a session reports Lighthouse performance ≥ 85 and AdSense Reports show impressions.
items.risk: If the banner never grants ad_storage (route A outside Europe), the units stay hidden by design: fix the banner, not the code.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: AdSense slots are set; run Lighthouse on an article with ads

items.title: Block sensitive ad categories and set ad load to Low
items.why: So no advertisement contradicts the calm, sourced register of an article.
steps: In AdSense open Brand safety, Content, Blocking controls, Sensitive categories. [verify in console]
Block: Dating, Drugs & supplements, Get rich quick, Politics, Religion, Sexual & reproductive health, Birth control, Cosmetic procedures, Astrology & esoteric, Weight loss, Significant skin exposure.
Under Ad serving set the Ad load slider to Low. [verify in console]
Save.
items.doneWhen: All eleven categories show Blocked and the ad load is Low.

phases.title: Play Console: app creation, store listing, forms, screenshots
phases.goal: The app exists in the Console with a complete store listing (Arabic and English), every declaration filled, and screenshots uploaded, ready to accept a first upload.

items.title: Create the app in Play Console
items.why: This creates the empty app record that the closed test, the listing and the forms attach to.
steps: In Play Console click 'Create app'.
Name: femio (written in lowercase Latin letters).
Default language: Arabic (Saudi Arabia). English, French and Spanish listings are added later.
Choose 'App' (not game) and 'Free'.
Accept the declarations and click Create app.
If the form asks for a package name, the app's id is the value in the paste box; otherwise it is taken from your first upload. [verify in console]
items.doneWhen: The Console Dashboard shows femio with its setup task list.
items.risk: The app name and package cannot be changed freely later; confirm the spelling before you click Create.

items.title: Ask a session to fill the support email, draft FR/ES, and lint the listing
items.why: The paste-ready texts still contain the placeholder [SUPPORT EMAIL: owner action 3], and the Console limits are hard (title 30, short 80, full 4,000).
steps: Tell a session your support email (the one from legal-placeholders) and ask it to replace the placeholder in docs/store/play-listing.en.md and docs/store/play-listing.ar.md.
Ask it to run pnpm store-lint; it measures every field, checks the lowercase femio wordmark and the required disclaimer, and fails on a leftover dagger mark.

D1 of the launch guide also adds French and Spanish listings, but docs/store holds only Arabic and English texts. Ask the session to draft French and Spanish from the English file for your review (translations are drafts until a native reader checks them).
Ask it to walk the Play reviewer checklist (disclaimer present, Data safety matches behaviour, no unproven claims, no keyword stuffing, no features missing from the build).
Read the Arabic and English files once yourself.
items.doneWhen: pnpm store-lint passes with no placeholder left, and you have read both texts.

items.title: Paste the Arabic and English store listing, category and contact details
items.why: This is what a woman in Riyadh or Cairo reads before installing.
steps: Open the Console menu Grow users, Store presence, Store listings (the launch guide calls it Main store listing). [verify in console]
Open the Arabic default listing. Paste the app title and the short description from docs/store/play-listing.ar.md.
Paste the full description from the same file. Keep the 'not a medical device' paragraph; Google requires it.
Add the English listing: paste title, short and full description from docs/store/play-listing.en.md.
Category: Health & Fitness. Tags: choose up to five from Play's fixed list: Period tracker, Pregnancy, Fertility, Women's health, Health tracking (exact labels may differ). [verify in console]
Contact email: the support email from legal-placeholders. Privacy policy URL: https://femioapp.com/ar/privacy.
Optional: custom store listings by country so Egypt and Saudi Arabia see the Arabic text. [verify in console]
Click Save.
items.doneWhen: The Arabic and English listings and the contact details are saved with no red warnings.

paste.label: Arabic short description (68)
paste.value: تتبّعي الدورة والتبويض والحمل بخصوصية تامة. سجلاتكِ تبقى على هاتفكِ.

paste.label: English short description (79)
paste.value: Private period, ovulation & pregnancy tracker. Your records stay on your phone.

items.risk: Titles carry no words like free, best or #1 and no emoji (Play metadata policy). Do not edit the wording in the Console; change the file via a session so the repo stays the source.

items.title: Ask a session to produce the eight screenshots per language
items.why: Most visitors never scroll past the first three screenshots, and they must show only real screens of the real build.
steps: Say to a session: 'Make the eight Play screenshots, Arabic set first, from the release candidate'. The launch guide says it renders them with flutter test --update-goldens at 1080x1920 or larger.

Captions go in the top third in the Dusk Bloom style; real app screens with synthetic data; no photos of people. The eight captions are in docs/store/play-listing.en.md and 04_GROWTH_PACK.md section 4.4.
Open a few images and check them against the app on your phone.
items.doneWhen: You have eight Arabic and eight English images that match the shipped app and the captions.
items.risk: docs/store/README.md says screenshots come from a real phone, while the launch guide says golden tests. Pick one: golden renders are quicker; a real phone is more honest. Either way, no feature absent from the build.

items.title: Upload the screenshots, icon and feature graphic
items.why: The listing cannot be reviewed without graphics.
steps: Ask a session to make the 1024x500 feature graphic: the lowercase wordmark femio at the start, then one line, nothing else (English: 'Your records never leave your phone.' Arabic: 'سجلاتكِ لا تغادر هاتفكِ.'), text inside the central safe area.
In Store listings open the graphics section of the Arabic listing. Upload the eight Arabic screenshots in order.
Upload the feature graphic and the app icon apps/web/public/icons/icon-512.png.
Repeat for the English listing with the English images.
Save.
items.doneWhen: Both listings show 8 screenshots, the icon and the feature graphic.
items.risk: Play may crop the feature graphic's edges or overlay a play button if a video is attached; keep text central. Exact image size rules: [verify in console].

items.title: Fill the simple App content forms (privacy, ads, access, audience, others)
items.why: Play will not accept an upload until every App content form is complete and true to the build.
steps: Open the Console, Policy, App content. [verify in console]
Privacy policy: https://femioapp.com/ar/privacy.
Ads: choose 'No, my app does not contain ads'.
App access: all features available without special access or sign-in.
Target audience: 18 and over only; tick 'restrict minor access'; answer No to 'appeals to children'.
Government apps, Financial features, News: No.
items.doneWhen: Each of these forms shows as complete in App content.
items.risk: Re-read each question in the Console: Google changes the wording.

items.title: Complete the content rating questionnaire (IARC)
items.why: Google needs a rating before the app can be published.
steps: In App content open Content rating and start the questionnaire. [verify in console]
Answer literally for an educational reference app: no violence, no gambling, no purchases, no user-generated content, no location sharing, no chat.
For the sexual-content question remember the app is reproductive-health education, not entertainment.
Submit and accept whatever rating results; do not steer it.
items.doneWhen: The Console shows a content rating certificate for femio.
items.risk: The expected rating is not verified [NEEDS CHECK on the day]. Never guess answers to get a lower rating.

items.title: Fill the Data safety form: nothing collected, nothing shared
items.why: A mismatch between this form and the app is a rejection and a trust failure. The answers are true only while the app has no INTERNET permission and no data-sending package; the build gate enforces both.
steps: In App content open Data safety.
Does your app collect or share any required user data types? No.
Data types: select none. Do not tick Health info only because the app is about health.
Do you provide a way for users to request deletion? Yes: Settings, 'Delete everything on this phone'.
Independent security review: No.
Privacy policy URL: https://femioapp.com/en/privacy (Arabic: /ar/privacy).
Save and submit.
items.doneWhen: Data safety shows complete with 'No data collected' and 'No data shared'.
items.risk: If Play later says Data safety mismatch, tell a session: 'Play says Data safety mismatch'; it re-runs the privacy tripwire.

items.title: File the Health apps declaration
items.why: Required for every track including the closed test. Under-declaring is the main risk.
steps: In App content open Health apps. [verify in console]
Select Period tracking under Health and fitness.
Select Reproductive and sexual health and Medical reference and education under Medical.
Do NOT select Medical device apps, Clinical decision support, or Disease prevention. Do NOT choose 'My app doesn't provide any health features'.
Check that the description contains the required disclaimer, then save.
items.doneWhen: The Health apps declaration shows complete with exactly those three features.
items.risk: Play rejects with 'Health apps declaration' if a feature is missing: reopen and tick the three.

phases.title: First test upload: build, closed test, 12 testers, 14 days, production access
phases.goal: A signed bundle runs on your phone and on 12 or more testers' phones for 14 days in a row, Google grants production access, and the app is live in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Ask a session to build the release candidate APK and bundle
items.why: Play wants an .aab bundle; your phone and testers outside Play use the .apk. The version code must rise on every upload.
steps: Open Claude Code in the femio repo.
Say: 'Build the release candidate APK and bundle for R4.12'.
The session checks no wip branches exist, runs pnpm gate, flutter analyze and flutter test, bumps the version in apps/mobile/pubspec.yaml, and builds both files.
It tells you where the files are.
items.doneWhen: Both files exist at the paths in the paste box and the session reports the gate passed.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: Build the release candidate APK and bundle for R4.12

items.risk: Without key.properties the release signs with the debug key: a test APK works, but Play will not accept the bundle.

items.title: Install the test APK on your phone
items.why: Your phone is the real test.
steps: Copy app-release.apk to your phone by USB cable, or send it to yourself.
Open it on the phone. Android warns about an unknown source: allow it once.
Install and open femio.
items.doneWhen: femio opens on your phone.
items.risk: Only install a file a session built for you; never an APK from anywhere else.

items.title: Run the six checks on your phone and report what is wrong
items.why: Each round of reports is one session; the goal is a phone you could hand to your wife or sister without explaining.
steps: Fresh install, onboarding in Arabic, first prediction, and the 'Private by design' notice.
Settings: set a PIN, kill the app, reopen: lock screen; wrong PIN refused; right PIN opens.
Settings: save a backup, pick a folder; the file femio-backup-<date>.femio exists.
Settings: delete everything, confirm, onboarding again, restore from the backup with the passphrase: the record is back.
Airplane mode throughout: nothing changes.
Both themes, Arabic and English; a 2.5-year-old phone if available.
Send each problem to a session in one message, for example: 'On the Today screen in Arabic, ...'.
items.doneWhen: You would hand this phone to your wife or sister without explaining anything.
items.risk: Each fix needs a new version code; a session handles that.

items.title: Run the Play Billing check once on your phone
items.why: Premium will be sold through Google Play Billing. A session proved the signed build carries no INTERNET permission even with the billing library inside (its telemetry was stripped). What only a phone can show is whether the library complains about that.
steps: Connect the phone (USB debugging on), signed in to Google Play.
In the repo: cd apps/mobile, then flutter run --profile.
In the app: Settings, About, tap 'femio Plus · billing check'. Read the line it shows.
In a second terminal: adb logcat | findstr /i "billing SecurityException transport" for 30 seconds while tapping once more.
Send a session the line the app showed and any SecurityException line, or 'none'.
items.doneWhen: The tile says 'Play Billing reachable: yes' (the product line says 'not found yet' until femio_plus exists) and logcat shows no SecurityException naming INTERNET.
items.risk: A SecurityException naming INTERNET means the billing library cannot live without the permission; premium then moves to the alternatives in ADR-076 and the session tells you.

items.title: Recruit 16 testers and collect their Gmail addresses
items.why: A personal account needs at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 days. Aim for 16, because a tester who leaves and rejoins restarts the 14-day clock.
steps: Create a Google Group named femio-testers (groups.google.com) and note its address (name@googlegroups.com).
Copy the recruitment message from 04_GROWTH_PACK.md section 5.5 (Modern Standard Arabic, Egyptian Arabic for WhatsApp, and English).
Replace [link] with the group join link, and check the dates in the text (11 to 25 November) still match your real start date.
Send it to friends, family, colleagues and your clinic's staff. Adults only.
Ask each person for the Gmail address they use on their Android phone.
Keep a list of who has joined; stop at 16.
items.doneWhen: At least 16 people have joined the group and you have their Gmail addresses.
items.risk: They must keep the app installed the whole time; testers may enter made-up data because nothing leaves the phone.

items.title: Create the closed test and upload the bundle
items.why: This starts the 14-day clock and puts the app on your testers' phones through Google Play.
steps: Check that the listing, Data safety, Health apps declaration and content rating are complete; the first upload is refused otherwise.
Open Test and release, Testing, Closed testing. [verify in console]
Click 'Create track' and name it femio closed.
Upload app-release.aab built by a session.
Release notes, two lines in Arabic and two in English.
Open Manage track, Testers: add the testers' emails as an email list, or add the Google Group address, and click Save changes.
Enter a feedback email or URL (it shows on the opt-in page).
Click Start rollout.
Copy the opt-in link and send it to every tester.
Ask a session to write the start date in docs/33_REBUILD_V3/PROGRESS.md line R5.4.
items.doneWhen: The track shows the release as Available and every tester has the opt-in link.
items.risk: The opt-in link only appears when the app status is Published. Group members must join the group before opting in. If a tester sees 'not available in your country', add the country under Testing, Countries.

items.title: Keep 12 or more testers opted in for 14 days in a row
items.why: Google's rule for new personal accounts: 12 testers opted in continuously for at least 14 days. A tester who leaves and rejoins restarts that count.
steps: Every week open the Console: Testing, Closed testing; the tester count must stay at 12 or more.
Send every tester message to a session as written, for example: 'Mona says the Hijri date is one day off'.
The session fixes, runs the gate, bumps the version and tells you when a new bundle is ready.
Upload the new bundle to the same track (Create new release). Updates do not restart the 14 days; uninstalls do.
Remind testers once at about day 7 to keep the app installed.
items.doneWhen: Day 14 passes with 12 or more testers still opted in.
items.risk: Dropping below 12 restarts the window. That is why you recruited 16.

items.title: Apply for production access on day 15
items.time: 30 min + about 7 days of waiting · free
items.why: Google must approve a new personal account before the app can go to everyone.
steps: On day 15 open the app's Dashboard in Play Console and click 'Apply for production' (the launch guide says 'Apply for production access'). [verify in console]
Fill the three sections: About your closed test, About your app/game, About your production readiness.
Describe the test honestly: who the testers were, what you fixed, what the app does.
Click Apply at the end of the final section.
items.doneWhen: The Console shows the application as submitted, and later as approved (usually about seven days).
items.risk: Clicking Discard or leaving a page before Next or Apply can erase what you wrote: write the answers in a note first and paste them.

items.title: Create the production release for Egypt and Saudi Arabia
items.why: This is the moment the app becomes installable by strangers.
steps: When approved, open Production and click 'Create release'.
Upload the latest app-release.aab.
Countries: Egypt and Saudi Arabia first (add others later).
Review and click Roll out.
items.doneWhen: A stranger in Riyadh can search femio on Google Play and install it.

items.title: Ask a session to wire the Play link into the website
items.why: Until the link is set, every Get the app button on the site falls back to the hand-off page.
steps: Copy your app's Play URL.
Say: 'The app is live at <Play URL>; wire the store link'.
The session sets PLAY_STORE_URL in apps/web/src/lib/site.ts and redeploys.
Click Get the app on a few pages.
items.doneWhen: Every Get the app button on femioapp.com opens the Play listing.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: The app is live at <Play URL>; wire the store link

items.title: Start the first-100-women plan (six weeks)
items.time: 6 weeks · a few hours a week
items.why: The target is real women, not vanity numbers; you measure with Play Console installs and the feedback link, not with analytics in the app.
steps: Read 04_GROWTH_PACK.md section 5 once: channels, calendar and the one-question feedback link.
Put QR cards in the clinic (each with its own ref tag).
Open the WhatsApp Channel and post to Egyptian Facebook groups, following each group's rules.
Publish three posts a week, each tied to one article or calculator.
Have the Ramadan set live by 11 January 2027.
Each week open Play Console acquisition reports and note installs by country and source.
items.doneWhen: Week 6: Play Console shows installs and retained installers, and you have read the feedback answers.
items.risk: Targets such as 200 installs by end of January are hypotheses, not facts.

phases.title: Social accounts, Canva and growth routines
phases.goal: Canva and every social account exist under the same handle, the growth routines are scheduled, and you know how to answer them in a few minutes a week.

items.title: Create the Canva account and have a session build the templates

Open Claude Code and say: 'Build the femio Canva templates (G3)'.

Upgrade to Pro only if it says it needs Brand Kit or Magic Resize.

items.why: One handle everywhere makes the brand easy to find. The wordmark is always the Latin lowercase femio.
steps: Try the handle femioapp on every platform (the plain femio is likely taken). Keep the same handle everywhere.
Use the Arabic-then-English bio in the paste box.
Add the site link with ?utm_source=<platform>&utm_medium=social (replace <platform> with instagram, tiktok and so on).
Write every handle on your 'femio growth' page.

items.title: Create the Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and X accounts
items.time: 35 min over a few days · free
items.why: Snapchat and Instagram reach the most women in Egypt and Saudi Arabia; X is for Saudi threads only.
steps: Instagram (10 min): create a Professional (Creator or Business) account with the handle, bio and link. Connect it to the Facebook Page from the meta item.

items.title: Create the WhatsApp Channel from your phone
items.why: A Channel is the quietest way to reach women who already use WhatsApp daily.
steps: On your phone open WhatsApp, Updates.
Tap Create channel, name it femio.
Add the bio.
Share the invite link and write it on your 'femio growth' page.

items.title: Join the Egyptian TTC, PCOS and ICSI Facebook groups
items.why: That is where the first 100 women already talk. Join as yourself, Dr Khaled, not as a brand.
steps: From your personal profile search for the Egyptian trying-to-conceive, PCOS and ICSI groups and request to join.
Read each group's rules before posting anything.
Follow the channel plan in 04_GROWTH_PACK.md section 5.1 row 3.

items.title: Start the growth routines and learn the weekly review
items.time: 20 min once, then about 45 min a week · free
items.why: Seven scheduled agents research, draft and report. Nothing goes live until you say publish.
steps: Open Claude Code (desktop app) and say: 'Create the growth routines from docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/routines'.
The session creates R1 (Monday 07:00 Cairo), R2 (Tuesday 07:00), R5 (Wednesday 07:00), R6 (first Friday 07:00) and R7 (Sunday 18:00) and shows you the list.

items.title: Spend an hour on your phone with Flo, Clue and one Arabic app

In each, count the ad units on an article and on a calculator.
Note where the paywall appears.
Write the counts into docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/reports/2026-10-28-competitor-monetization.md section 2.
items.doneWhen: Section 2 of that report holds your counts for all three apps.

phases.title: Premium (after launch): payments profile and femio_plus
phases.goal: AFTER LAUNCH, planned for February 2027 before app release 2: Google can pay you, the femio_plus subscription exists with monthly and yearly plans, and a test purchase works.

items.title: After launch: create the Play payments profile
items.why: Google needs your merchant identity and bank before it can sell a subscription for you. Egypt is a supported merchant country.
steps: Open Play Console, Setup, Payments profile (the Console's exact menu may differ). [verify in console]
Click 'Create payments profile'.
Country Egypt; business type as your registration (KM Digital Labs).
Add your bank account in EGP and tax information.
Submit and wait; Google verifies within days.
items.doneWhen: The payments profile shows as verified.
items.risk: Do this in February 2027, after launch, not before it.

items.title: After launch: create the femio_plus subscription with monthly and yearly plans
items.why: One product with two base plans lets Play handle upgrades and proration, and keeps the app free of accounts and servers.
steps: Open your app in Play Console, Monetize with Play, Products, Subscriptions (the guide writes Monetize, Products, Subscriptions). [verify in console]
Click 'Create subscription'. Product ID femio_plus (it cannot be changed or reused). Name: femio Plus (keep the Latin wordmark, also in Arabic).
Add the description from 02_MONETIZATION.md section 2.4 (Edit subscription details), then Save.
Add base plan with ID monthly: auto-renewing, billing period 1 month, grace period 7 days, account hold on.

Manage country availability, then set prices: base USD 0.99. Read the EGP and SAR rows that Play shows; where Play's minimum is higher it will say so. Round by hand to local convention (for example 49 EGP and 3.99 SAR). Save, then Activate.
Add base plan with ID yearly: billing period 1 year, base USD 9.99, round EGP and SAR (for example 499 EGP and 37.99 SAR). Activate.
On the yearly plan click 'Add offer': free trial of 7 days, eligibility 'New customer acquisition' (new subscribers), then Activate.
items.doneWhen: Subscriptions lists femio_plus with two active base plans and the trial offer.
items.risk: Play fee on subscriptions is 15 percent per Google's page cited in 02_MONETIZATION.md; any later restructure is not verified. If a price is below the minimum for a country, set that row to the minimum Play shows.

items.title: After launch: add license testers so purchases are free during tests
items.why: You and two testers can try buying without paying.
steps: Open Play Console, Setup, License testing. [verify in console]
Add your own Gmail and two testers' Gmails.
Save.
items.doneWhen: Three addresses are listed under License testing.

items.title: After launch: ask a session to integrate Play Billing
items.why: The app must read the two plans from Google Play and restore purchases after a reinstall.
steps: Say: 'Premium products exist: femio_plus with monthly and yearly; integrate Play Billing (M4)'.
The session builds app release 2 and a bundle for the internal test.
Install the internal-test build on your phone.
Open Settings, femio Plus: both prices appear in EGP.
Make a test purchase, then reinstall the app and use restore.
items.doneWhen: Settings, femio Plus shows both prices in EGP on your phone, a test purchase completes, and it restores after reinstall.

phases.title: Monthly upkeep: ASO, reviews, data drops
phases.goal: Each month the store text follows the real search terms, every review gets a reply within 48 hours, and the routines receive their data.

items.title: Monthly ASO: read search terms and update the listing
items.why: Real search terms replace guesses; the title and short description matter most.
steps: Open Play Console, Store performance, Store listing acquisition (and Search terms when it appears). [verify in console]
Note the top terms by installs.
Tell a session: 'ASO monthly: here are the top terms'.
The session proposes changes to docs/store/play-listing.en.md and play-listing.ar.md, title and short description first. You answer publish.
Paste the new text into Store presence, Store listings and click Save; the change goes live with the next review. [verify in console]
Every quarter: if a screen changed, ask a session to re-render the eight screenshots at 1080x1920 from the golden tests and upload them under the listing's graphics.
items.doneWhen: The listing files in the repo and the Console text match, and the month's terms are recorded.

paste.label: Session sentence
paste.value: ASO monthly: here are the top terms

items.risk: Never add keyword lists or ranking words to the title (Play metadata policy).

items.title: Reply to every Play review in its own language within 48 hours
items.time: 10 min a few times a week · free
items.why: Replies build trust; medical questions always need the same safe answer.
steps: Open Play Console, Ratings and reviews. [verify in console]
Open the drafts that routine R6 prepared for the common cases.
Reply in the reviewer's language.
For any medical question reply 'talk to your doctor' and add the link to the matching article.
items.doneWhen: No review is older than 48 hours without a reply.

items.title: Feed the routines: weekly Play CSV and monthly feedback answers
items.why: The weekly report (R7) can only be as good as the numbers you drop in.
steps: Weekly: open Play Console, Statistics, Export report (installs and retention). [verify in console]
Save the CSV as docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/reports/play/YYYY-WW.csv (git-ignored; only summaries are committed), or tell a session 'Here is this week's Play CSV' and attach it.
Monthly: paste the one-question feedback answers into docs/34_GROWTH_OPS/reports/feedback/YYYY-MM.md after removing any health detail someone typed despite the warning.
items.doneWhen: This week's CSV and this month's feedback file exist.

items.title: Quarterly: decide whether the ad units stay
items.why: Ads only pay if the revenue per 1,000 impressions (RPM) is high enough; the plan's decision point is the first quarter's RPM.
steps: Open AdSense, Reports, and read the page RPM for the quarter.
If RPM is below 0.5 dollars, ask a session to remove the units and keep selling only the app.
If it is higher, keep the units and ask a session to run the page-speed check again (Lighthouse 85 or higher).
items.doneWhen: You have said keep or remove, and a session has recorded it.
items.risk: The month-3 revenue estimate of 6 to 18 dollars is a hypothesis with no data behind it yet.
